advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restore the explanatory comment on the `except RemovedInputError: raise` clauses in _mcp_startup_handshake.py so the deliberate (currently-redundant) re-raise is not mistaken for dead code.
evidence: Original (deleted from _mcp_health.py) carried: `# RemovedInputError subclasses BaseException so it already sails past the handler below; the re-raise is redundant today and exists so the intent survives a future widening of that handler.`
advisory.finding: The extracted `run_startup_handshake` and `install_startup_handshake` reduced the `except RemovedInputError: raise` comment to a bare `raise` with no explanation. The original explained the re-raise is deliberate (RemovedInputError subclasses BaseException so it already bypasses the broad handler; the re-raise is redundant today but preserves intent against a future widening of the `except Exception` handler). Without that comment, a future maintainer may delete the seemingly-dead `except X: raise` and silently reintroduce the swallow.
advisory.suggested_fix: Re-add the two-line rationale comment above each `raise` explaining that RemovedInputError subclasses BaseException and the re-raise guards against a future widening of the broad handler.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Carry over the precedence-and-LIMIT docstrings for select_probe_host / _declared_public_host into _mcp_startup_handshake.py so the guard-facing host-selection logic remains documented.
evidence: New docstring reduced to one line: `"""The Host header the startup handshake presents to this server's own guard."""` (src/rebar/_mcp_startup_handshake.py:68)
Original carried a multi-paragraph docstring enumerating precedence rules 1-4 and the explicit LIMIT clause (deleted from _mcp_health.py in the diff)
_declared_public_host similarly reduced to one line at src/rebar/_mcp_startup_handshake.py:42
advisory.finding: The extracted `select_probe_host` and `_declared_public_host` lost their detailed docstrings that documented the security-relevant host-selection precedence (declared public host, then literal allowlist entry, then port-wildcard, then bind-address loopback fallback) and the stated LIMIT that a deployment with no declared public URL cannot verify the allowlist. These functions carry non-obvious guard-facing logic; the terse replacement docstrings make the precedence and its intentional limitation invisible to future maintainers.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the back-import guard to also reject `import rebar._mcp_health` / `import rebar._mcp_serving` module-form imports, not only the `from ... import` form.
evidence: ABSENCE: no assertion covers `import rebar._mcp_health` (module-form) or `importlib`/aliased imports
assert "from rebar._mcp_health import" not in source
assert "from rebar._mcp_serving import" not in source

ABSENCE: no behavioral acyclicity check — the invariant 'the leaf has no back-imports from the facade' is asserted only against source text, so `import rebar._mcp_health` (module form), an aliased import, or a function-local deferred import would evade the grep while still forming a dependency.
advisory.finding: The new guard test `test_handshake_leaf_exists_without_back_imports` only checks for the `from rebar._mcp_health import` / `from rebar._mcp_serving import` substrings. A plain `import rebar._mcp_health` (module-form import) or an aliased import would pass the test while still creating the back-import the test intends to forbid, so the acyclic-constraint guard is incomplete.
merged_from: test_handshake_leaf_exists_without_back_imports asserts on the TEXT of the module under test (substring absence of import statements) rather than its behavior; it is a source-grep change-detector that breaks on a behavior-preserving import-form change and misses a cycle introduced via a bare/aliased/deferred import.
